I will do it much like last year, with only small changes. I farm only 2 mu, and I do most of it by myself, so I will not do anything fancy. I look first at what worked on my own land, then I look at what the neighbors do. Around here, if wheat or maize looks hungry and I try to save too much on fertilizer, I lose grain, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. Since I have well water, I will not let the crop sit dry at the key times. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer in, then add more nitrogen when it starts to stand up and grow fast in spring. I will water it about 3 times if the weather is normal. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people do, give it a solid base dressing, then topdress nitrogen around knee-high to waist-high growth, and water 2 times if rain is not enough. I will spray when I see weeds, aphids, armyworms, rust, or leaf disease starting, usually 2 times each crop in a normal year. I will keep the land worked with rotary tillage because on 2 mu that is the easiest for me, and it leaves the ground fine enough for sowing. I am aiming for a steady harvest, not gambling to save one bag of fertilizer.
